subject: Retention cadence sync — backup purge windows, subprocessor handoff & EU transfer mapping
messages:
From: Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@luminahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-05 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Initial: retention windows + cross-border backups

Marcus —

Quick intro: I'm Arjun on the data security team at LuminaHealth. We're finalizing our procurement checklist for Redwood and I need clarity on a couple of operational items before we proceed to legal:

1) Backup purge cadence — do you support a documented, auditable purge run (not just logical deletion) for backups containing PII? We need an estimate of how long an item may persist in immutable/nearline backups after a deletion request.
2) Subprocessor change notice & handoff — how are notifications handled for new subprocessors who may process EU personal data?
3) Cross-border map — can you provide a simple mapping of which backups/replicas may cross EU borders and which remain EU-only?

If you can share a draft timeline and any supporting artifacts (matrix, proposed DPA language) that would speed our legal review. We have a procurement deadline May 20.

Thanks,
Arjun Patel
Senior Security Engineer
LuminaHealth

--
LuminaHealth (external)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-05 11:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial: retention windows + cross-border backups

Hi Arjun — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and I attached a short timeline and a subprocessor matrix for the exact services.

1) Backup purge cadence:
- Logical deletion happens immediately on request (or via DSR).
- Immutable/archival backups follow our scheduled purge runs: standard cadence is 90 days from logical deletion for nearline snapshots; a secondary cold snapshot tier is retained for up to 540 days depending on customer profile (we can carve EU-only shorter).
- We provide an auditable run log for each purge (timestamp, objects targeted, operator id). See tab "PurgeRuns" in the attached XLSX.

2) Subprocessor notices:
- We provide 30 days notice prior to adding any new subprocessor that will process EU personal data; notice includes the role, location, and the expected data flows.
- For higher-risk subprocessors (e.g., managed SIEM, backup-hosting in third-party cold storage) we engage with Lumina legal for review and will offer contract language or mitigations.

3) Cross-border mapping:
- Primary serving region options: EU-only (Frankfurt/Amsterdam) or multi-region (US+EU).
- Backups: by default snapshots are region-paired; however "global snapshots" used for disaster recovery may cross borders. The attached matrix marks each backup type with a transfer flag.

Next steps: Kim (Legal Ops) and Karthik (Data Protection) copied — can you confirm whether Lumina requires a strict EU-only backup policy, or if region pairing with documented cross-border controls is acceptable? If EU-only, we'll propose a DPA amendment and a 30-day plan to switch your account to EU-only archival lanes.

Attachments: redwood-backup-purge-timeline.xlsx, subprocessor_matrix_v4.csv

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@luminahealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-06 08:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial: retention windows + cross-border backups

Arjun / Marcus — adding a couple of DPA/operational notes from our side.

- DPA language: recommended clause to propose for EU-only carveout: "Customer may elect EU-only archival lanes. Upon election, Redwood will re-route all archival snapshot writes to EU-only storage and revoke global snapshot replication for that Customer within 30 days." We will prepare a tracked-change DOCX.
- Purge proof format: Legal prefers a signed CSV export (purge id, object id hashes, deletion timestamp, operator) plus a hash of the export stored in our evidence ledger. That will satisfy audit teams.
- Subprocessor mitigation: For subprocessor additions we can offer a temporary compensating control: disable cross-border cold snapshot replication for the affected namespaces during the 30-day notice period.

Action for Karthik: please prepare the short amendment language and a one-pager showing how the 30-day carve-in affects restore windows (i.e., how long a customer can request restores from cold tier after the carve).

Kim
Director, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Dunne <sara.dunne@luminahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Lumina Legal <lumina-legal@luminahealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-07 14:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial: retention windows + cross-border backups

Thanks Marcus — helpful. A few clarifying Qs from legal/security after reviewing the matrix and timeline:

1) For customers who elect EU-only archival lanes, what is the maximum RTO for restores from the cold tier if an object is requested for deletion but litigation hold is later asserted? We need both the expected and the worst-case time.
2) Is the purge run manual or automated? If manual, what change controls / approver logs are retained?
3) Can we get a sample purge export (redacted) to assess the CSV format you mentioned?

Redlines we will propose:
- A clause limiting cross-border snapshot replication for Lumina to "disabled by default; enabled only with signed written consent from Lumina Legal".
- Add an SLA-style confirmation that purge audit exports will be delivered within 5 business days of request.

We are generally fine with the 30-day subprocessor notice but will want a commitment to consult on any subprocessor that would host cold backups outside the EU.

If possible, can we get a short call next week to finalize the DPA amendment language? A 30-minute slot Tue/Wed preferred.

Best,
Sara Dunne
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
LuminaHealth

--

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Dunne <sara.dunne@luminahealth.com>, Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@luminahealth.com>

Date: 2028-05-10 10:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial: retention windows + cross-border backups

Sara / Arjun — thanks for the precise redlines. Agreed items and next steps below.

Agreed / proposed:
- EU-only archival lane: we will provide an account-level toggle; turning it on will disable global replication for archival snapshots within 30 calendar days. Expected RTO from cold tier: 48-72 hours in normal operations; worst-case (cross-region rehydration) 7 business days. We'll include fallback options (expedited restore) as billable runbooks if you need faster recovery.
- Purge runs: automated scheduled jobs produce purge manifests. Final object removal from cold tier is executed by automation but gated by a verification step (signed approval token). All approver & operator metadata is recorded in the manifest and retained in the evidence ledger.
- Purge export sample: attached a redacted CSV (sample row format) in the XLSX and will provide a full sample via secure share after NDA scoping.
- DPA amendment draft: Karthik will circulate tracked changes by EOD Monday; Kim to coordinate the contractual language for the cross-border toggle.

Planning call: Tue 2028-05-16 09:00 UTC / 10:00 CET works for our team. I'll send a calendar invite and include a short agenda (timeline, DPA clause, sample purge export deliverable).

Deliverables & owners:
- Karthik: DPA tracked changes (deadline: 2028-05-14)
- Marcus: secure sample purge export + updated XLSX with purge manifest schema (deadline: 2028-05-12)
- Kim: draft EU-only archival toggle contract text + sign-off plan (deadline: 2028-05-14)

Please confirm the meeting slot and whether Lumina needs additional attendees (procurement or InfoSec ops).

Thanks — Marcus
